## Onyx Lora Caption Generator

**Class:** `OnyxLoraCaptionGeneratorNode` · **Category:** `image` · output node

Generate LoRA training captions for all images in a folder.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |

| `provider` | Dropdown: `gemini`, `vertex`, `grok` | yes | `gemini` |  |  |
| `trigger_word` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  |  |
| `mode` | Dropdown: `sdxl` | yes | `sdxl` |  | sdxl: caption style for SDXL person LoRA training (no face/hair/identity, focus on outfit/scene/lighting/framing). |
| `gemini_model` | Dropdown: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash` | no | `gemini-3.6-flash` |  |  |
| `vertex_json_folder` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | Folder of service-account .json files, for provider=vertex. The first one is used; api_key is ignored in that mode. |

| `caption_instruction` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | Optional override. If empty, mode determines the prompt. |
| `temperature` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.7` | 0.0 – 2.0 (step 0.05) |  |
| `max_tokens` | `INT` | no | `8192` | 64 – 8192 (step 64) |  |

_No outputs (saves files / side effects only)._

## Onyx Video Frame Extractor

**Class:** `OnyxVideoFrameExtractorNode` · **Category:** `image`

Extract one frame from a video file or from a connected frame sequence.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `video` | Dropdown: `(no videos found)` | yes | — |  |  |
| `start_second` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.0` | 0.0 – 86400.0 (step 0.1) |  |
| `frame_count` | `INT` | yes | `10` | 1 – 9999 (step 1) | How many frames are sampled, and therefore how far selected_frame can reach. |
| `frame_interval` | `INT` | yes | `1` | 1 – 300 (step 1) | Take one frame every N. 1 samples every frame. |
| `selected_frame` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 9998 (step 1) | Which sampled frame to output. 0 with start_second=0 gives the very first frame. |
| `video_frames` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Connect the `video` output of Onyx Image and Video Batch Loader.<br>When connected it REPLACES the file dropdown entirely — nothing is read from disk. |
| `video_fps` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 240.0 (step 0.01) | Frame rate of the connected frames, so start_second can be turned into a frame index. Left at 0, start_second is ignored. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  |

## Onyx Image Blur (batched)

**Class:** `OnyxImageBlurBatched` · **Category:** `image/postprocessing`

Blur a long image batch in slices, so the 32-bit index limit never applies.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` | yes | — |  |  |
| `blur_radius` | `INT` | yes | `1` | 1 – 31 (step 1) |  |
| `sigma` | `FLOAT` | yes | `1.0` | 0.1 – 10.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `frames_per_slice` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 4096 (step 1) | 0 = auto: the largest slice that stays under PyTorch's 2^31-element indexing limit, computed from this batch's own resolution.<br>Set it lower by hand only to cut VRAM peaks further. |

## Onyx Face Dataset Prompts

**Class:** `OnyxFaceDatasetPrompts` · **Category:** `Onyx`

Face-only dataset prompts for Nano Banana Pro (image 1 = the girl). Each queue run outputs the next angle; queue the workflow 'total' times to get the full set. append_prompt adds your own text at the end of every prompt.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `expressions` | Dropdown: `mixed (12)`, `mixed x2 (24)`, `neutral only (12)` | yes | `mixed (12)` |  | mixed: one expression per angle (4 neutral, 3 subtle smile, 3 smile, 2 kiss), never teeth.<br>mixed x2: a second pass of the 12 angles with the expressions shifted (24 prompts). |
| `mode` | Dropdown: `sequential`, `fixed index` | yes | `sequential` |  | sequential: each run outputs the next prompt and loops at the end.<br>fixed index: always outputs the prompt at 'index' (to redo one shot). |
| `index` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 999 | Start position (sequential) or the prompt to output (fixed index). Changing it restarts the sequence from there. |
| `extra_text` | `STRING` | no | — |  | Optional text appended to every prompt (e.g. a trigger word). |
| `run_token` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  |  |
| `age` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 99 | Age of the person in image 1. 0 = not mentioned. Otherwise every prompt ends with 'She is N years old.' |
| `append_prompt` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | Text added at the END of every prompt, for every generation (after the age sentence). Leave empty to add nothing. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `prompt` | `STRING` |  |
| `label` | `STRING` |  |
| `index` | `INT` |  |
| `total` | `INT` |  |

## Onyx Image and Video Batch Loader

**Class:** `OnyxImageBatchLoader` · **Category:** `Onyx`

Sequential batch loader for images and videos. Upload via the node UI, then click Queue All. Each queue run outputs the next item: images leave through `image`, videos through `video` + `video_fps` + `duration` + `frame_count` + `audio`. Trim and frame rate are applied per clip, using each clip's own real values.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `batch_data` | `STRING` | yes | `{}` |  |  |
| `video_max_side` | `INT` | yes | `1024` | 0 – 4096 (step 64) | Longest edge of the decoded video frames. 0 keeps native size.<br>A 15 s 1080p clip is 360 frames, over 2 GB held as float32 RGB. The cap keeps a normal phone video from taking the machine down.<br>Irrelevant for images, which are never resized. |
| `trim_mode` | Dropdown: `seconds`, `frames` | yes | `seconds` |  | Whether the trim below is expressed in seconds or in frames. |
| `trim_start` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.0` | 0.0 – 100000.0 (step 0.01) | Where each clip starts. 0 keeps the beginning. |
| `trim_end` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.0` | 0.0 – 100000.0 (step 0.01) | Where each clip ends. **0 means the end of the video**, so the same setting works across clips of different lengths — which is the whole point of trimming in a batch.<br>Set 8 with trim_mode=seconds to keep the first 8 seconds of every clip, whatever its duration. |
| `resize_method` | Dropdown: `none`, `maintain aspect ratio`, `stretch to fit`, `pad`, `crop` | yes | `none` |  | How each clip is fitted to custom_width x custom_height.<br>maintain aspect ratio: fits inside the box, output size varies with each source's ratio.<br>stretch to fit: exact size, distorts.<br>pad: exact size, black bars, nothing lost.<br>crop: exact size, no distortion, edges lost.<br><br>Use pad or crop when every clip must come out the same size — 'maintain aspect ratio' does not guarantee that across a batch of mixed sources. |
| `custom_width` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 8192 (step 8) | 0 derives the width from the height and the source ratio. |
| `custom_height` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 8192 (step 8) | 0 derives the height from the width and the source ratio. |
| `force_fps` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.0` | 0.0 – 240.0 (step 0.01) | Resample every clip to this frame rate. 0 keeps each clip's native rate.<br>Set 24 to normalise a batch of mixed 30 and 60 fps sources — MiniMax H3 works at 24, and a clip left at 30 plays back at the wrong speed. |
| `consume_on_load` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `False` |  | ON: an item disappears from the list as soon as it has been loaded. A crash three quarters of the way through a batch then costs you only what had not run yet — re-queue and it carries on instead of starting over.<br>The file itself is NOT deleted from disk, only removed from this node's list.<br>Pair it with queue_batch_size = 1: an item is consumed when it is LOADED, not when the graph finishes, so anything still queued behind a failure is lost from the list. |
| `queue_batch_size` | `INT` | yes | `50` | 1 – 50 (step 1) | How many runs 'Queue All' submits at a time.<br>50 is fastest. 1 is the safe setting: a failure then costs one item instead of everything already sitting in the queue.<br>With consume_on_load ON, the button waits for the queue to empty between batches — it has to, because each run rewrites the list the next submission is built from. |
| `minimax_15s_limit` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | MiniMax H3 takes at most 15 s of reference video.<br>ON: a clip between 15 s and 16.5 s (after trim) is cut to 15 s by dropping its end. A clip longer than 16.5 s is skipped — cutting it would remove real content — and the next item loads in its place. Images are not affected. |
| `video_first_frame` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | ON: for each video, ONLY its first frame is output, through `image` (photos keep coming out of `image` too, in sequence). The video is not decoded as a whole: one frame is read at the trim start, then Max side / resize are applied. `video` and `audio` stay empty.<br>OFF: normal video loading; `image` is a 64x64 placeholder for videos. |
| `max_frames` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 100000 (step 1) | Frame load cap: maximum number of frames kept per clip, after trim and force_fps. 0 = no limit. Same role as frame_load_cap in VHS Load Video. |
| `width` | `INT` | no | — |  | Overrides Width (custom_width) when connected. |
| `height` | `INT` | no | — |  | Overrides Height (custom_height) when connected. |
| `fps` | `FLOAT` | no | — |  | Overrides Force fps when connected (0 = native). |
| `frame_load_cap` | `INT` | no | — |  | Overrides Frame load cap when connected (0 = no limit). |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `video` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `video_fps` | `FLOAT` |  |
| `duration` | `FLOAT` |  |
| `frame_count` | `INT` |  |
| `audio` | `AUDIO` |  |
| `video_info` | `VHS_VIDEOINFO` |  |

| `multiplier` | `INT` | yes | `2` | 1 – 16 | 2 doubles the frame count: 24 fps in, 48 fps out. |
| `storage` | Dropdown: `RAM (float32, one allocation)`, `memory-mapped file (lowest RAM)` | yes | `RAM (float32, one allocation)` |  | RAM: one float32 tensor. Already half the original node's peak, because nothing is concatenated.<br>memory-mapped: the array lives in a temp .npy instead. Resident memory stays near zero — use it when the output alone does not fit, and when the next node reads the batch in order (a video encoder does). |
| `fast_mode` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  |  |
| `ensemble` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  |  |
| `scale_factor` | Dropdown: `0.25`, `0.5`, `1.0`, `2.0`, `4.0` | yes | `1.0` |  |  |

| `batch_size` | `INT` | yes | `1` | 1 – 64 | Interpolated frames per GPU call. Costs VRAM, not host RAM. |
| `clear_cache_after_n_frames` | `INT` | yes | `10` | 1 – 1000 | Empties the CUDA cache every N pairs. This only ever concerned VRAM — the failure this node fixes was host RAM, after the loop. |

Needs ffmpeg (PATH or imageio-ffmpeg). |

'random' picks a model per file. |

## Onyx Segment Cache

**Class:** `OnyxSegmentCache` · **Category:** `Onyx`

Cache a rendered segment on disk. On a re-run, a matching segment is read back and its sampler is never executed.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `segment_index` | `INT` | yes | — |  | Connect the Segment node's `next_index` MINUS nothing — use the same index that drove this segment. Segment 1's node emits 1. |
| `session` | `STRING` | yes | `chain` |  | One name per job. Change it and you start a fresh cache; reuse it and a re-queue picks up where the last one died. |
| `mode` | Dropdown: `read + write`, `write only (force re-render)`, `off (passthrough)` | yes | `read + write` |  | read + write: reuse a matching segment, otherwise render and keep it.<br>write only: always re-render, and overwrite what is stored — use this when you changed something the fingerprints cannot see, like a seed.<br>off: this node does nothing at all. |
| `precision` | Dropdown: `uint8 (smallest, 8-bit output)`, `float16 (keeps grading headroom)` | yes | `uint8 (smallest, 8-bit output)` |  | uint8: ~0.75 GB per 243-frame segment at 768x1344.<br>float16: twice that, and keeps values a later grade could use. |
| `cache_version` | `INT` | yes | `1` | 1 – 9999 (step 1) | Bump this by one whenever you change something the fingerprint image cannot see — a seed, steps, cfg, the intent text.<br>It is the manual half of the key, and it is manual on purpose: the alternative is hashing the compiled prompt, which an LLM rewrites on every run, so the cache would never hit at all. |
| `images` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | The sampler's output. LAZY: on a cache hit this is never evaluated, so the sampler does not run. |
| `audio` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  |  |
| `fingerprint_image` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Connect the Segment node's `reference_slice`. This is what makes a hit trustworthy: change the source video and the key changes with it.<br>Leave it empty and the cache trusts the index alone. |
| `fingerprint_text` | `STRING` | no | — |  | For DETERMINISTIC text only.<br>Do NOT connect the Context-IR's compiled `prompt`: an LLM rewrites it on every run, so the key would change every time and the cache would never hit. The node refuses it and warns if you do. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `images` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `audio` | `AUDIO` |  |
| `was_cached` | `BOOLEAN` |  |
| `info` | `STRING` |  |

## Onyx Temporal Mask Smooth

**Class:** `OnyxTemporalMaskSmooth` · **Category:** `Onyx`

Stabilizes a MASK batch from SAM3 video propagation: temporal median, closing, dilate, gaussian blur — in that order. Processed in memory-bounded chunks, so long clips don't blow up RAM/VRAM.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `masks` | `MASK` | yes | — |  |  |
| `temporal_radius` | `INT` | yes | `2` | 0 – 15 |  |
| `closing_radius` | `INT` | yes | `3` | 0 – 64 |  |
| `dilate_radius` | `INT` | yes | `10` | 0 – 128 |  |
| `blur_radius` | `INT` | yes | `5` | 0 – 128 |  |
| `threshold` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.5` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `frames_per_slice` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 4096 (step 1) | 0 = auto : la plus grande tranche qui reste sous le budget memoire (limite d'indexation 32 bits + budget de 1 GiB), calculee depuis la resolution et les rayons de ce batch.<br>A baisser a la main seulement si le pic memoire est encore trop haut. |
| `opening_radius` | `INT` | no | `2` | 0 – 64 | Erode puis dilate (dans cet ordre), AVANT le closing. Supprime les petits blobs isoles que la median temporelle n'a pas filtres (rares faux positifs de detection SAM3) : un blob plus petit que ce rayon disparait a l'erosion et ne revient pas au dilate — contrairement au closing (dilate puis erode), qui reconnecte/comble mais ne supprime rien. Augmente si des artefacts isoles persistent, 0 pour desactiver. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `mask` | `MASK` |  |

## Onyx Conditioning Cache (text encode)

**Class:** `OnyxConditioningCache` · **Category:** `Onyx/Conditioning`

Drop-in replacement for CLIP Text Encode in workflows with a fixed prompt. The first run encodes and saves; later runs (even after a restart) read the saved result and the text encoder is never loaded. Change the text (or the encoder / its LoRAs) and it encodes once more. Put it before ReferenceLatent / guide nodes. The cache folder is capped at 300 MB (oldest entries deleted first).

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `text` | `STRING` | yes | — |  | The prompt. Same text = no encoder load. |
| `cache_name` | `STRING` | yes | `klein_refiner` |  | Label of the cache files (only used to name them). |
| `clip` | `CLIP` | no | — |  | Text encoder (CLIPLoader). LAZY: only loaded when this prompt has never been encoded. Must be connected for the first run. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `conditioning` | `CONDITIONING` |  |

## Onyx Detailer

**Class:** `OnyxDetailer` · **Category:** `Onyx/Detailer`

Copie exacte de FaceDetailer (Impact Pack), meme options bbox/segm/sam, avec quatre ajouts : 'interpolation' (resampler du resize retour, defaut bicubic+antialias), 'sharpness' (unsharp mask luminance-only sur la zone regeneree), 'color_match_strength' (0-1, realigne moyenne/ecart-type par canal sur le crop d'origine) et une entree optionnelle 'segs' (SEGS deja calculees en amont, ex: par un masque manuel) qui remplace entierement la detection bbox/sam/segm quand elle est connectee -- 'bbox_detector' devient alors facultatif.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` | yes | — |  |  |
| `model` | `MODEL` | yes | — |  | Si `ImpactDummyInput` est connecte au model, l'etape d'inference est sautee. |
| `clip` | `CLIP` | yes | — |  |  |
| `vae` | `VAE` | yes | — |  |  |
| `guide_size` | `FLOAT` | yes | `512` | 64 – <nodes.MAX_RESOLUTION> (step 8) |  |
| `guide_size_for` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  |  |
| `max_size` | `FLOAT` | yes | `1024` | 64 – <nodes.MAX_RESOLUTION> (step 8) |  |
| `seed` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – max |  |
| `steps` | `INT` | yes | `20` | 1 – 10000 |  |
| `cfg` | `FLOAT` | yes | `8.0` | 0.0 – 100.0 |  |
| `sampler_name` | Dropdown (list filled by ComfyUI) | yes | — |  |  |
| `scheduler` | Dropdown (list filled by ComfyUI) | yes | — |  |  |
| `positive` | `CONDITIONING` | yes | — |  |  |
| `negative` | `CONDITIONING` | yes | — |  |  |
| `denoise` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.5` | 0.0001 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `feather` | `INT` | yes | `5` | 0 – 100 (step 1) |  |
| `noise_mask` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  |  |
| `force_inpaint` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  |  |
| `bbox_threshold` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.5` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `bbox_dilation` | `INT` | yes | `10` | -512 – 512 (step 1) |  |
| `bbox_crop_factor` | `FLOAT` | yes | `3.0` | 1.0 – 10 (step 0.1) |  |
| `sam_detection_hint` | Dropdown: `center-1`, `horizontal-2`, `vertical-2`, `rect-4`, `diamond-4`, `mask-area`, `mask-points`, `mask-point-bbox`, `none` | yes | — |  |  |
| `sam_dilation` | `INT` | yes | `0` | -512 – 512 (step 1) |  |
| `sam_threshold` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.93` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `sam_bbox_expansion` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 1000 (step 1) |  |
| `sam_mask_hint_threshold` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.7` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `sam_mask_hint_use_negative` | Dropdown: `False`, `Small`, `Outter` | yes | — |  |  |
| `drop_size` | `INT` | yes | `10` | 1 – <nodes.MAX_RESOLUTION> (step 1) |  |
| `cycle` | `INT` | yes | `1` | 1 – 10 (step 1) |  |
| `interpolation` | Dropdown: `bicubic`, `bilinear`, `nearest-exact`, `nearest`, `area` | yes | `bicubic` |  | Resampler utilise pour le resize retour (paste-back) apres decode VAE. Impact Pack original n'expose pas ce choix. |
| `sharpness` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.5` | 0.0 – 2.0 (step 0.05) | Nettete (unsharp mask, luminance uniquement) appliquee apres le resize retour, sur la zone regeneree seulement. 0 = desactive. 0.3 = subtil, 0.5-0.6 = marque, 1.0+ = agressif. |
| `color_match_strength` | `FLOAT` | yes | `1.0` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.05) | Force du color-match statistique (moyenne/ecart-type par canal) qui realigne la teinte/luminosite de la zone regeneree sur celle du crop d'origine. 0 = desactive, 1 = match complet. |
| `bbox_detector` | `BBOX_DETECTOR` | no | — |  | Detecteur bbox (visages/yeux). Facultatif si `segs` est connecte : dans ce cas, la detection bbox/sam/segm est entierement sautee et ces SEGS sont utilisees telles quelles. |
| `segs` | `SEGS` | no | — |  | SEGS deja calculees (ex: un masque manuel converti en SEGS). Si connecte, remplace entierement la detection bbox/sam/segm : `bbox_detector` et les reglages bbox_*/sam_* sont ignores. |
| `sam_model_opt` | `SAM_MODEL` | no | — |  |  |
| `segm_detector_opt` | `SEGM_DETECTOR` | no | — |  |  |
| `detailer_hook` | `DETAILER_HOOK` | no | — |  |  |
| `inpaint_model` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  |  |
| `noise_mask_feather` | `INT` | no | `20` | 0 – 100 (step 1) |  |
| `scheduler_func_opt` | `SCHEDULER_FUNC` | no | — |  |  |
| `tiled_encode` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  |  |
| `tiled_decode` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  |  |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `cropped_refined` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `cropped_enhanced_alpha` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `mask` | `MASK` |  |
| `detailer_pipe` | `DETAILER_PIPE` |  |
| `cnet_images` | `IMAGE` |  |

## Onyx H3 VFX LoRA

**Class:** `OnyxH3VfxLora` · **Category:** `Onyx/H3`

Loads the MiniMax H3 VFX LoRA for the chosen mode (vfx_edit, edited first frame, style_transfer) onto the H3 model and outputs its trigger word. Use the SAME mode as on H3 Context-IR. Wiring: source video frames -> MiniMaxH3AddGuide (frame_idx 0) between the conditioning and the sampler; the edited first frame or the style image -> the reference image slot. Needs ComfyUI v0.34+.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `model` | `MODEL` | yes | — |  |  |
| `vfx_mode` | Dropdown: `none`, `vfx_edit`, `vfx_edit (edited first frame)`, `style_transfer` | yes | `vfx_edit` |  | MiniMax H3 only. Edit the connected source VIDEO instead of generating from references. Needs the matching LoRA loaded (Onyx H3 VFX LoRA node) and the source video wired into MiniMaxH3AddGuide (ComfyUI v0.34+).<br>• vfx_edit — change something in the clip ("make the jacket red"). Reference images are not used and are not analysed.<br>• vfx_edit (edited first frame) — retouch frame 0 yourself, connect it as image_1: H3 propagates the retouch through the whole clip.<br>• style_transfer — restyle the clip; image_1 = optional style reference.<br>The prompt gets the trigger word, and <Video 1> becomes "the source video". |
| `strength` | `FLOAT` | yes | `1.0` | -2.0 – 2.0 (step 0.05) | LoRA strength. 1.0 = as trained. Lower it if the edit spills onto parts of the clip that should not change. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `model` | `MODEL` |  |
| `trigger` | `STRING` |  |

## Onyx Face Mask

**Class:** `OnyxFaceMask` · **Category:** `Onyx/Image`

Covers every face of the image with a solid shape, detected with YuNet, the same way the Face Swap automation masks its second image.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` | yes | — |  |  |
| `score_threshold` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.7` | 0.1 – 0.99 (step 0.01) | YuNet confidence. 0.7 is what the Face Swap automation uses. If nothing is found, a second attempt is made at 0.35. |
| `margin` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.39` | 0.0 – 1.5 (step 0.01) | Extra area around the detected face box, as a fraction of its width / height on each side. 0.39 = the automation's value (covers forehead, hair line and chin). |
| `min_face_size` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.05` | 0.0 – 0.5 (step 0.005) | Faces smaller than this fraction of the image's short side are ignored (5 % in the automation). |
| `shape` | Dropdown: `square`, `ellipse` | yes | `square` |  | square = the automation's black rectangle. ellipse = rounder, keeps more of the corners of the box. |
| `color` | Dropdown: `black`, `white`, `gray` | yes | `black` |  |  |
| `fail_if_no_face` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | Off: an image with no face comes out unchanged (with a warning in the console). On: the run stops with an error. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `mask` | `MASK` |  |
| `faces_found` | `INT` |  |

## Onyx Content Remaker

**Class:** `OnyxInstagramFaceSwapNode` · **Category:** `Onyx/NanoBanana` · output node

Onyx Content Remaker Downloads posts from Instagram, Threads or Pinterest and runs the face swap automation on every image. Fallback chain: Nano Banana Pro → Nano Banana 2.1 → Nano Banana 2 → Seedream 5 Pro → GPT Image 2. Low-light + blurry images can be routed to GPT Image 2 first. Already processed images are skipped on re-run (resume support).

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `face_reference` | `IMAGE` | yes | — |  |  |
| `source_url` | `STRING` | yes | `https://www.instagram.com/username/` |  | Instagram, Threads or Pinterest URL.<br>• Instagram : https://www.instagram.com/username/<br>• Threads   : https://www.threads.net/@username/<br>• Pinterest : https://www.pinterest.com/username/ or /username/board/ |
| `output_folder` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  | Folder where swapped images will be saved. A sub-folder named after the account will be created. |
| `max_posts` | `INT` | yes | `50` | 0 – 9999 (step 1) | Maximum number of image posts to process. 0 = all. |
| `provider` | Dropdown: `WAVESPEED`, `GOOGLE`, `FAL`, `KIE`, `VERTEX` | yes | `WAVESPEED` |  | API provider. GPT Image 2 only works on KIE / FAL / WAVESPEED. |
| `use_nano_banana_pro` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  |  |

Image and video generation / editing in one node: Nano Banana Pro / 2 / 2.1, Seedream, GPT Image, Veo 3.1, Kling, Wan, Seedance and Omni, through Google, Vertex, WaveSpeed, Kie.ai, fal.ai or Atlas Cloud. The badge above the node shows the estimated API cost of the next run.

| `disable_safety_threshold` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `True` |  | Disable the safety filter (on by default). Turn off to use the provider's stricter default thresholds. |

| `batch_size` | `INT` | no | `1` | 1 – 10 (step 1) | Number of images to generate in parallel |

| `system_instructions` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | [GOOGLE / VERTEX] System instructions |
| `video_duration` | `INT` | no | `8` | 3 – 15 (step 1) |  |
| `video_generate_audio` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `True` |  | [Video] Generate audio track. Supported by all Veo providers. |
| `aspect_ratio` | Dropdown: `auto`, `1:1`, `2:3`, `3:2`, `3:4`, `4:3`, `4:5`, `5:4`, `9:16`, `16:9`, `21:9` | no | `auto` |  | auto = détecte l'aspect ratio des images en input et sélectionne le plus proche parmi les ratios supportés. Fallback 1:1 si aucune image en input. |
| `temperature` | `FLOAT` | no | `1.0` | 0.0 – 2.0 (step 0.1) | [GOOGLE / VERTEX] Model creativity |
| `top_p` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.95` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.05) | [GOOGLE / VERTEX] Nucleus sampling |
| `fal_safety_tolerance` | Dropdown: `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6` | no | `6` |  | [FAL NB] 1 = strict \| 6 = permissive (default) |

Ignored on other models.<br>• GPT Image 2.0 (FAL): low / medium / high — xhigh & max fall back to high.<br>• GPT Image 2.5 Flare / Sunburst (FAL, WaveSpeed): low → max.<br>  Higher tiers add detail and cost noticeably more.<br>• Kie.ai has no quality setting for GPT Image 2.5 (ignored). |
| `image_1` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Main source image |
| `image_2` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Image source 2 |
| `image_3` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Image source 3 |
| `image_4` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Image source 4 |
| `image_5` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Image source 5 |
| `video_reference` | `AB_VIDEO` | no | — |  | [Kling 3.0 Motion Control] Connect an 'Onyx Video Loader' node.<br>The duration of the generated video will match the reference.<br>[Seedance 2.0 / Reference mode] Also accepted as a motion reference (max 15s). Rejected in First & Last Frame mode.<br>[Omni Flash / Edit mode] The video to edit. Required in that mode, refused in the other two — Omni does accept a video reference in its schema, but the model does not actually process it yet. |
| `audio_reference` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  | [Seedance 2.0 / Reference mode] Audio reference — drives rhythm, or lip-sync when the prompt asks for it. Max 15s.<br>Rejected in First & Last Frame mode, and ignored by every other model.<br>[Omni Flash] Never accepted — the API takes no audio input at all. Omni generates its own soundtrack; describe it in the prompt instead. |
| `video_input_mode` | Dropdown: `First & Last Frame`, `Reference`, `Edit (video, Omni)` | no | `First & Last Frame` |  | [Seedance 2.0 / Omni Flash] These modes are mutually exclusive in the APIs themselves — you cannot mix them.<br><br>First & Last Frame<br>  Seedance: image_1 becomes the first frame, image_2 the last.<br>  Omni Flash: image_1 becomes the first frame. A second image is refused — Omni has no frame interpolation.<br>  Video and audio inputs are refused.<br><br>Reference<br>  Seedance: up to 5 images, 1 video and 1 audio guide style, motion and rhythm freely.<br>  Omni Flash: up to 6 images. No video, no audio.<br>  No guarantee on the first/last frame.<br><br>Edit (video, Omni)<br>  Omni Flash only: send an existing video plus an edit instruction ("make the phone invisible"). Keep the prompt simple and add "Keep everything else the same". Refused by every other model. |
| `video_mode_enabled` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | [Video] Enabled by JS toggle — do not modify manually. |
| `face_swap_enabled` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | [Automation] Enabled by JS block — do not modify manually. |
| `breast_refiner_enabled` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | [Automation] Enabled by JS block — do not modify manually. |
| `low_neck_enabled` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | [Automation] Enabled by JS block — do not modify manually. |
| `amateur_mode_enabled` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | [Automation] Amateur, Low quality input match — overrides the default face swap prompt. |
| `face_expression` | `STRING` | no | `Neutral` |  | [Automation] Facial expression — managed by JS block — do not modify manually. |
| `face_swap_custom_prompt` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | [Automation] Extra prompt appended to the face swap prompt — managed by JS block — do not modify manually. |
| `max_black_retries` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 10 (step 1) | Replay the generation when the provider returns a black image (a failed generation). 0 disables it.<br><br>The retry has to happen here, not in a downstream check node: ComfyUI's graph is acyclic, so nothing that receives the black image can re-trigger what produced it. Retrying in-process also keeps a batch loader in step — it never sees the failed attempt.<br><br>The whole call is replayed, so a partly-black batch re-generates its good images too. Each attempt is billed. |
| `atlascloud_api_key` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | [ATLASCLOUD] Atlas Cloud API key (Nano Banana Pro / 2 / 2.1 only). |
| `cache_mode` | Dropdown: `off`, `reuse identical request` | no | `off` |  | off (default): every run calls the provider and is billed — re-running the same prompt gives a new variation.<br>reuse identical request: if this exact request (same prompt, settings and input pixels) was already generated, the saved result is returned instantly and nothing is billed. Change anything — even one word or the seed — and it generates again.<br>Results are kept in the pack's _cache/api_cache folder (oldest removed past 3 GB). |

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `images` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `video` | `STRING` |  |
| `grounding_sources` | `STRING` |  |

## Onyx Renoise

**Class:** `Onyx_Renoise` · **Category:** `Onyx/Post-Processing`

Onyx Renoïse Injects authentic digital camera sensor noise. Select an ISO preset — from ISO 0 (off) to ISO 6400 (very strong grain). Night Mode adds chroma-heavy noise for a low-light look. Optional 'look' / sliders: phone high-ISO rendering — fine grain, luma mottle, purple/green chroma blotches, noise-reduction smear, colour bleed and degradation, JPEG.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` | yes | — |  |  |
| `seed` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – max |  |
| `iso_preset` | Dropdown: `ISO 0 (Off)`, `ISO 50`, `ISO 100 (Clean)`, `ISO 200`, `ISO 400`, `ISO 800`, `ISO 1600`, `Night Mode`, `ISO 3200`, `ISO 6400` | yes | `ISO 400` |  | ISO noise level. ISO 0 = off \| ISO 50 = barely visible \| ISO 100 = clean \| ISO 1600 = heavy grain \| ISO 3200/6400 = very heavy \| Night Mode = chroma-heavy. |
| `grain_size` | `FLOAT` | yes | `1.0` | 0.1 – 8.0 (step 0.1) | Taille des grains de bruit (PAS l'intensite, qui vient de l'ISO preset). 1.0 = pixel par pixel (comportement d'origine). Au-dessus de 1 = grains plus gros/visibles (bruit genere a resolution reduite puis agrandi en nearest-neighbor). En dessous de 1 (jusqu'a 0.1) = grain plus fin/serre (bruit genere a resolution superieure puis moyenne vers le bas). |
| `look` | Dropdown: `Manual`, `Phone low light (iPhone indoor)`, `Phone night (heavy)`, `Phone indoor (subtle)` | no | `Manual` |  | Recette complete 'photo de telephone' (grain + taches chroma + lissage NR + couleurs degradees + JPEG). Manual = utilise les reglages ci-dessous. Avec un look, les reglages manuels sont ignores (look_strength reste actif). Conseil : iso_preset sur 'ISO 0 (Off)' ou 'ISO 200' avec un look, sinon les deux bruits s'additionnent. |
| `look_strength` | `FLOAT` | no | `1.0` | 0.0 – 5.0 (step 0.05) | Multiplicateur global du bruit (grain fin, marbrures, taches chroma), en Manual comme avec un look. 0 = pas de bruit, 1 = normal, 2 = double, 5 = maximum. Avec un look, il dose aussi le lissage, la bavure, la degradation des couleurs et le JPEG. |
| `fine_grain` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 0.25 (step 0.001) | Grain fin pixel par pixel (luminance). 0.01 = realiste, 0.03 = fort. |
| `grain_color` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.25` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.05) | Part du grain fin qui est coloree (0 = grain monochrome, 1 = grain RVB independant). |
| `mottle` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 0.25 (step 0.001) | Marbrures de luminance basse frequence (le 'bruit' par dessus le grain, typique des capteurs de telephone apres reduction de bruit). |
| `chroma_blotch` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 0.35 (step 0.001) | Taches de couleur basse frequence (violet / vert / magenta). C'est l'effet 'zones de couleurs differentes' d'un ISO eleve. 0.009 = realiste (calibre sur une vraie photo), 0.02 = bien visible, 0.05 = extreme. |
| `blotch_size` | `FLOAT` | no | `5.0` | 2.0 – 96.0 (step 0.5) | Taille des taches (marbrures + chroma) en px pour une image de 2000 px de cote (adapte automatiquement a la resolution). |
| `purple_green` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.55` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.05) | Teinte des taches : 0 = toutes les teintes, 1 = uniquement axe violet <-> vert (le plus typique des capteurs de telephone). |
| `shadow_weight` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.7` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.05) | Concentration du nouveau bruit dans les ombres (0 = uniforme, 1 = presque que dans les ombres). |
| `nr_smear` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.05) | Lissage 'reduction de bruit' de telephone : efface la micro-texture dans les zones plates (peau cireuse) en gardant les contours. |
| `chroma_bleed` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 8.0 (step 0.1) | Bavure des couleurs de l'image (flou de la chroma seule, comme le 4:2:0 et le debruitage chroma). En px pour 2000 px. N'attenue plus les taches de bruit. |
| `color_degrade` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 2.0 (step 0.05) | Degradation des couleurs : ombres desaturees, noirs releves et legerement olive, hautes lumieres ternes. Au-dessus de 1 = exagere. |
| `jpeg_quality` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 100 (step 1) | Recompression JPEG reelle (0 = desactive). 75-85 = rendu photo de telephone partagee. |
| `onyx_post` | `ONYX_POST` | no | — |  | From Onyx Studio (post output) or Onyx Post Style. A look other than 'none' overrides this node's settings. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  |

## H3 Context-IR (Gemini)

**Class:** `OnyxH3ContextIR` · **Category:** `Onyx/Prompt`

Local rebuild of the H3 cloud preprocessing stage. Pass A reads the real media and reports facts as JSON; pass B compiles that JSON plus your intent into an H3 prompt, using the official MiniMax guides verbatim as its system prompt.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `intent` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  | Keep this SHORT, and write only what must CHANGE. The official Context-IR calls send one sentence — 'Pull focus to the people in the background and add more steam to the ramen bowl.' The media are read for everything else; describing the scene here competes with what pass A actually observed. |
| `duration_seconds` | `FLOAT` | yes | `8.0` | 2.0 – 15.0 (step 0.1) | Target length. The official API takes this as a Context-IR input, not just a generation parameter: shot count, pacing and where beats land all depend on it. A prompt written blind to duration plans a timeline the render cannot hold. |
| `aspect_ratio` | `STRING` | yes | `adaptive` |  | Target framing: adaptive, 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 21:9, 3:2, 2:3, 5:4, 4:5.<br>'adaptive' is the official default and lets the compiler follow the media. Connect the aspect_ratio output of Onyx Resolution (MP) to keep it in sync with what you actually render. |
| `target_model` | Dropdown: `MiniMax H3`, `Seedance`, `Seedance v2`, `MiniMax H3 Endless`, `Seedance Severed`, `Seedance 2 Recreate (extreme jiggle)`, `Seedance 2 Recreate (extreme jiggle, outfit from ref)`, `Seedance 2.5 Recreate (extreme jiggle)`, `Seedance 2.5 Recreate (extreme jiggle, outfit from ref)`, `Seedance 2 Recreate (strong jiggle)`, `Seedance 2 Recreate (strong jiggle, outfit from ref)`, `Seedance 2.5 Recreate (strong jiggle)`, … (30 options) | yes | `MiniMax H3` |  | Which video model the prompt is written for.<br>MiniMax H3: compiles against the two official MiniMax guides, verbatim, with <Picture N> / <Video N> labels.<br>MiniMax H3 Endless: same guides, written for long videos rendered in ONE pass (15-30 s+): one continuous take, action beats every 3-5 s, each speaker's speech in a single <d> block and one sentence fixing the voice for the whole clip.<br>Seedance: compiles against ByteDance's six-slot grammar with @Image 1 / @Video 1 tags.<br>Seedance v2: same tags, but outputs one structured JSON object (people, scene_events with measured dialogue, a single continuous shot, negative_prompt, reference_images).<br>Seedance Severed: universal prose template for swapping the woman of a reel with ANY character, no audio and no dialogue (the original soundtrack is put back afterwards). Wire image_1 = three-view face sheet (front / three-quarter / profile) and image_2 = body + outfit sheet with the head masked, plus the video (color-inverted copy recommended).<br>Natural Prompting Seedance ...: no video. Write your idea in plain words in intent (any language); image_1 = the person. 'outfit from prompt' = the outfit you describe in intent; 'outfit from ref' = the outfit of image_2. Same jiggle registers and outfit rule as Recreate. Duration = duration_seconds (0 = 10 s), adaptive aspect = 9:16.<br>Seedance Recreate Second pass (verify JSON): proofreads a first-pass Recreate JSON (in grounding_override) against the video and returns the corrected JSON; no reference images needed.<br>Seedance 2 / 2.5 Recreate (12 modes): ONE pass. The model watches the video itself (sent natively at video_analysis_fps on Gemini / Vertex) and writes the finished Seedance JSON that recreates it with another person: timing, dialogue, camera, light. Wire video (+ video_audio), image_1 = the new person's head (face + hair), image_2 = body (a single image is used for both). intent = optional extra notes; duration_seconds is ignored (the real video length is used). 2 = compact prompt, 15 s parts; 2.5 = full prompt, 30 s parts. Jiggle register: extreme = maximum soft-tissue physics, strong = pronounced but believable, normal = real intensity, no push. "outfit from ref" = the subject wears the outfit of image_2 (image_1 if single) instead of the source video's outfit. Best on Gemini 3.1 Pro with provider Gemini or Vertex.<br><br>The two are not interchangeable. H3's guide asks for an exhaustive description; ByteDance's says a long paragraph fights itself and that two or three sentences is the target. Pass A does not change — it describes media, not a destination. |
| `provider` | Dropdown: `Gemini`, `Vertex`, `Grok`, `Kie` | yes | `Gemini` |  |  |
| `model` | Dropdown: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `grok-4.20-0309-reasoning`, `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning`, … (17 options) | yes | `gemini-3.6-flash` |  |  |
| `guide_folder` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  | Leave empty (default): the two official MiniMax guides are built into the pack, nothing to link or install.<br>Only fill this in to override them with a locally edited copy — point it at a folder holding VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_base_en.md and VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md. |
| `max_tokens` | `INT` | yes | `8192` | 512 – 65536 (step 512) |  |
| `image_1` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Reference image. Slots are labelled in order: the first connected slot becomes <Picture 1>, the next <Picture 2>, and so on. Skipping a slot never leaves a gap in the numbering. |
| `image_1_role` | Dropdown: `reference`, `first_frame`, `last_frame` | no | `reference` |  | What image_1 is FOR, mirroring the official Context-IR payload.<br>reference: a picture of the subject.<br>first_frame: this image IS the opening frame of the render.<br>last_frame: this image IS the closing frame.<br><br>This is not a mode selector — you describe the asset, the compiler still decides the mode on its own. |
| `image_2` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_2_role` | Dropdown: `reference`, `first_frame`, `last_frame` | no | `reference` |  | Same as image_1_role. Set image_1 to first_frame and image_2 to last_frame for a first-and-last-frame render. |
| `image_3` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_4` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_5` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_6` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  |  |
| `images_batch` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Optional extra images as a batch, appended AFTER the numbered slots. Useful with the Onyx Image Batch Loader. |
| `video` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Source video frames, labelled <Video 1>. Sampled to 8 timecoded keyframes. |
| `video_fps` | `FLOAT` | no | `24.0` | 1.0 – 120.0 (step 0.01) | Used to write the timecode on each keyframe. Wrong here means wrong shot boundaries. |
| `media_resolution` | Dropdown: `default`, `low`, `medium`, `high` | no | `low` |  | Token budget per image sent to pass A. Gemini 3: 1120 at default, 280 at low — a factor of four on every keyframe.<br>Google recommends low for action recognition and description, which is what the video frames are for. Raise it only if the grounding starts missing wardrobe or face detail, and consider spending the saving on more keyframes instead. |
| `video_keyframes` | `INT` | no | `8` | 2 – 32 (step 1) | How many frames of the video pass A actually looks at.<br>The compiler writes the action sequence from these and nothing else, so this sets the resolution of the timeline it can describe. 8 over a 15 s clip is one frame every 1.9 s — enough to say what happens, not enough to say exactly how.<br>Roughly one per second is a good target. Each frame costs vision tokens, so raise it for long or busy clips, not for everything. |
| `video_audio` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  | The soundtrack that belongs to the video above. It is described as part of <Video 1>, not as a separate asset.<br>This is what fills overall_soundscape with dated events instead of a generic line. |
| `ref_audio_1` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  | A standalone audio reference, labelled <Audio 1> — a voice timbre to follow, a music bed, a sound to reproduce. Separate from the video's own soundtrack, exactly as reference_audio is separate from reference_video in the official payload. |
| `ref_audio_2` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  | Second standalone audio reference, <Audio 2>. |
| `gemini_api_key` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  |  |
| `grok_api_key` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | xAI key (console.x.ai), for provider=Grok.<br>Audio assets are not sent to Grok: its image input is documented and already used elsewhere in this pack, its audio input is not verified. Use Gemini or Vertex when the soundtrack matters. |
| `vertex_json_folder` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  |  |
| `grounding_override` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | Paste a corrected grounding JSON to skip pass A entirely and recompile without another vision call.<br><br>Seedance Recreate Second pass (verify JSON): put the JSON produced by the first Recreate pass HERE (paste it, or wire the first node's text output into this widget). It is proofread against the video; the same video / video_audio / provider / model must be connected. Reference images and intent are not needed (intent = optional notes). |
| `window_start_seconds` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 3600.0 (step 0.001) | Where this render starts inside the supplied source, in seconds.<br>Leave at 0 for a normal one-shot render.<br>For a chained render, give every segment the SAME full video and only change this: the grounding is then computed once and served from cache, and each segment gets its own window with timestamps re-based to zero.<br>Added LAST on purpose: ComfyUI serialises widget values by position, so inserting it higher would shift every widget in already-saved workflows. |
| `pinned_lead_seconds` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 60.0 (step 0.001) | How many seconds at the START of this render are already fixed by a guide, and must therefore NOT be described.<br>For a chained render: connect the Segment node's `guide_seconds`. Those frames are pinned by AddGuide — image AND audio — so any line of dialogue the compiler places inside them is rendered a second time and then thrown away by the Join. That is what makes a character repeat a sentence across a seam.<br>The timeline origin does not move: 00:00.000 stays the first frame of the render, because H3 encodes time absolutely and the frames really are being generated. Only the DESCRIPTION starts later. |
| `transcribe_speech` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | Runs gemini-3.5-transcribe on the soundtrack first and gives both passes the MEASURED start and end time of every spoken word.<br>Pass A is a vision pass: asked when a line is spoken it reads keyframes and estimates, and it estimates badly. This replaces the guess with a measurement.<br>REQUIRES a gemini_api_key: it uses the Interactions API, which is documented on the Gemini API and which I could not confirm on Vertex. Without a key the pass is skipped and the node behaves exactly as before.<br>Costs one call per soundtrack for the whole render — it is cached on disk beside the grounding, so a four-segment chain transcribes once. |
| `extra_prompt_rules` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | OFF restores the Pass B prompt to the shape it had for the render you judged near-perfect, before a week of accumulated rules.<br><br>What it removes:<br>• 'Never write stillness' — 1464 characters that were always on<br>• the 'Render window' block on segment 1 (segments 2+ keep theirs, they need the re-basing)<br><br>Each rule fixed something real. What was never measured is their combined effect: they stack in the same context as the official guide, and the compiler averages them. Turn them back on one at a time if a defect they addressed comes back. |
| `keyframes_match_model` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | Samples the reference video EXACTLY as H3 does — every 12th frame at 24 fps, labelled 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 …<br><br>H3 hands its text encoder the video at 2 fps and nothing else (nodes_minimax_h3.py: range(0, n, FPS // 2)). Evenly spaced keyframes land on OTHER frames with OTHER labels, so a beat written at 00:07.333 points at an instant the model does not have — its strip only holds 7.0 and 7.5.<br><br>With this on, pass A describes the very images the model will see, and pass B is told to put action beats on the same 0.5 s grid.<br>video_keyframes is ignored: the stride belongs to the model. A 294-frame segment gives 25 frames either way, so it costs nothing. |
| `motion_from_video_only` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `False` |  | Stops the prompt from putting timestamps on physical actions.<br><br>In a reference-video render the footage already fixes WHEN every movement happens, frame by frame. A timestamp in the prompt is a SECOND answer to the same question — and it is an estimate: pass A reads keyframes and misjudges by around a second. The model then has two sources that disagree and splits the difference, which is what 'the same scene, played differently' looks like.<br><br>Turn this on for motion control. Dialogue keeps its timestamps: H3 generates the audio, so nothing else says when a line is spoken. |
| `kie_api_key` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | Kie.ai key, for provider=Kie: the Gemini models of the list, or grok-4-7 / 4-6 / 4-5 / 4-3, billed on your Kie.ai credits. |
| `video_analysis_fps` | `FLOAT` | no | `8.0` | 1.0 – 24.0 (step 1.0) | Seedance 2 / 2.5 Recreate: how many frames per second of the source video the model looks at. Gemini's default is 1 fps, which misses gestures, hair flips and lip movement; 8 is a good balance, 12-24 for very fast action (more tokens). Gemini / Vertex only: Grok and Kie receive up to 40 timestamped frames instead. |
| `seed` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – max | Re-roll control. Same settings + a new seed = a NEW analysis and a new prompt (the cache is bypassed and the seed is sent to Gemini / Vertex / Grok). Set the control to 'randomize' to get a different prompt on every run, or 'fixed' to compare settings with the same seed.<br>0 = legacy behaviour: results are cached per media, nothing is sent to the API. |
| `remove_observations` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `True` |  | Seedance Recreate modes write an "_observations" log first (one line per event seen, with its timestamp). It is for YOU to check what the model saw; Seedance must not receive it.<br>On: the key is removed from the JSON before it leaves the node. Off: kept (read it, then delete it yourself). |
| `gemini_thinking_mode` | Dropdown: `high`, `medium`, `low`, `minimal` | no | `high` |  | Gemini 3 thinkingLevel (Gemini and Vertex providers; ignored by other providers and by models older than Gemini 3). high = deepest analysis. A model that does not accept the chosen level is retried with its own default. |
| `vfx_mode` | Dropdown: `none`, `vfx_edit`, `vfx_edit (edited first frame)`, `style_transfer` | no | `none` |  | MiniMax H3 only. Edit the connected source VIDEO instead of generating from references. Needs the matching LoRA loaded (Onyx H3 VFX LoRA node) and the source video wired into MiniMaxH3AddGuide (ComfyUI v0.34+).<br>• vfx_edit — change something in the clip ("make the jacket red"). Reference images are not used and are not analysed.<br>• vfx_edit (edited first frame) — retouch frame 0 yourself, connect it as image_1: H3 propagates the retouch through the whole clip.<br>• style_transfer — restyle the clip; image_1 = optional style reference.<br>The prompt gets the trigger word, and <Video 1> becomes "the source video". |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `h3_prompt` | `STRING` |  |
| `grounding_json` | `STRING` |  |

## Onyx Grok Prompt Generator

**Class:** `OnyxGrokPromptNode` · **Category:** `Onyx/Prompt`

Send a text prompt (and optionally an image) to Grok and get a generated prompt back. Plug an Onyx Image Batch Loader into 'image' + Queue All to run one request per image in the batch.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `prompt` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  | The prompt/instruction to send to the model. |
| `model` | Dropdown: `grok-4.20-0309-reasoning`, `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning`, `grok-3`, `grok-3-fast`, `grok-3-mini`, `grok-3-mini-fast`, `grok-2-vision-1212` | yes | `grok-4.20-0309-reasoning` |  | xAI Grok model. Vision-capable models are listed first - use one of those if you connect an image. |
| `image` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Optional image (e.g. from the Onyx Image Batch Loader for batch runs). Sent alongside the prompt to vision-capable models. |
| `api_key` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | xAI API key (console.x.ai). Cached after first use. |
| `temperature` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.7` | 0.0 – 2.0 (step 0.05) | Creativity of the response (0 = deterministic, 2 = very creative). |
| `max_tokens` | `INT` | no | `1024` | 64 – 8192 (step 64) | Maximum number of tokens in the response. |
| `trigger_word` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | Replaces every occurrence of TRIGGER in the prompt. Left empty, TRIGGER is sent as-is. |
| `seed` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – max | randomize = a new Grok prompt on every run (e.g. every image of a batch). fixed = reuse the same prompt while nothing else changes. Not sent to the API. |
| `provider` | Dropdown: `xAI (Grok)`, `OpenRouter` | no | `xAI (Grok)` |  | xAI: direct call to api.x.ai with api_key and the 'model' list.<br>OpenRouter: call openrouter.ai with openrouter_api_key and openrouter_model (any OpenRouter model id). |
| `openrouter_api_key` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | OpenRouter key (openrouter.ai/keys, starts with sk-or-). Cached after first use. |
| `openrouter_model` | `STRING` | no | `x-ai/grok-4.1-fast` |  | OpenRouter model id, e.g. x-ai/grok-4.1-fast, google/gemini-2.5-flash, anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5. Empty = 'x-ai/' + the model chosen above. Pick a vision model if you connect an image. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `output_prompt` | `STRING` |  |

## Onyx Speed HD Sampler

**Class:** `OnyxSpeedHDSampler` · **Category:** `Onyx/Sampling`

Onyx Speed HD Sampler Spectral Progressive Diffusion — progressively expands the latent resolution during denoising for faster sampling with preserved quality. Connect the output to SamplerCustomAdvanced.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `base_sampler` | Dropdown | yes | `euler` |  | Underlying ODE solver. Any comfy k_diffusion sampler is supported. Multistep solvers restart at each transition because the schedule is segmented. |
| `transform` | Dropdown: `dct`, `dwt`, `fft` | yes | `dct` |  | Spectral basis used at each transition. DCT (default) supports any scale ratio; DWT requires consecutive scales to differ by exactly 2x (needs PyWavelets); FFT accepts any ratio. |
| `mode` | Dropdown: `delta_optimal`, `manual` | yes | `delta_optimal` |  | 'delta_optimal' computes transitions from 'scales', 'delta', and the selected power-spectrum preset. 'manual' uses user-specified sigma thresholds. |
| `model_preset` | Dropdown: `flux`, `wan21`, `custom` | yes | `flux` |  | Power-spectrum preset for delta-optimal mode. 'flux' and 'wan21' use measured (A, beta). 'custom' uses the manual spectrum_A / spectrum_beta inputs below. |
| `scales` | `STRING` | yes | `0.5,1.0` |  | Comma-separated resolution fractions ending at 1.0. Used in delta_optimal mode. Example: 0.5,1.0 or 0.25,0.5,1.0. |
| `delta` | `FLOAT` | yes | `0.01` | 0.0001 – 0.5 (step 0.001) | Noise-dominated tolerance. Smaller values transition later. |
| `manual_sigmas` | `STRING` | yes | `0.85` |  | Comma-separated sigma thresholds, one per transition (length = number of scales minus 1). Used in manual mode. Example for scales=0.25,0.5,1.0: 0.95,0.85. |
| `spectrum_A` | `FLOAT` | yes | `203.615097` | 0.0 – 1000000.0 (step 0.001) | Power-spectrum amplitude A (used when model_preset=custom). |
| `spectrum_beta` | `FLOAT` | yes | `1.915461` | 0.0 – 10.0 (step 0.001) | Power-spectrum decay exponent beta (used when model_preset=custom). |
| `seed` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 2147483647 (step 1) | Seed for the spectral-noise padding at each transition. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `sampler` | `SAMPLER` |  |

Mute or bypass one named group from a single toggle. Acts on the canvas, not during execution.

| `enabled` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `True` |  | Off applies the mode below to every node in the group. |
| `off_mode` | Dropdown: `mute`, `bypass` | yes | `mute` |  | mute: the group does not run, and nothing downstream of it runs either.<br>bypass: the group is skipped but its inputs are passed through to its outputs, so the rest of the graph keeps working around it.<br><br>Use bypass on a group sitting in the middle of a chain, mute on a branch that ends in its own output. |

## Onyx H3 Frame Snap

**Class:** `OnyxH3FrameSnap` · **Category:** `Onyx/Utils`

Snap a frame count to a length MiniMax H3 can generate without realigning it. Prevents the tail H3 invents when it rounds the target up and the reference down.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `frame_count` | `INT` | yes | `198` | 1 – 3600 (step 1) | Plug the frame count coming out of your video loader. |
| `alignment` | Dropdown: `Video + Audio (17k+5 and 40Hz)`, `Video only (17k+5)` | yes | `Video + Audio (17k+5 and 40Hz)` |  | Video + Audio: only lengths that sit on H3's 17k+5 video grid AND land exactly on its 40 Hz audio clock (39, 90, 141, 192, 243...). Use this whenever the clip has speech - it is what keeps lip sync locked to the last frame.<br>Video only: the full 17k+5 grid (5, 22, 39, ... 192, 209...). Finer granularity, but the audio stream can drift over the tail. |
| `rounding` | Dropdown: `nearest (may exceed source)`, `down (never exceed source)` | yes | `nearest (may exceed source)` |  | nearest: pick the closest valid run, above or below. Overshoot is capped at half a grid step (25 frames on the audio-aligned grid, 8 on the video grid) and those extra frames are simply trimmed from the result.<br>down: never exceed the source. Safer on paper, but on the audio-aligned grid missing a run by a few frames costs a full 51-frame step - over two seconds of video for the sake of four missing frames. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `frames` | `INT` |  |
| `seconds` | `FLOAT` |  |

| `positive` | `CONDITIONING` | yes | — |  |  |

| `sampler_name` | Dropdown (list filled by ComfyUI) | yes | `lcm` |  |  |
| `scheduler` | Dropdown (list filled by ComfyUI) | yes | `simple` |  |  |
| `segment_length` | `INT` | yes | `81` | 5 – 321 (step 4) | Frames generated per segment, snapped to 4k+1. |
| `max_frames` | `INT` | yes | `0` | 0 – 100000 | Hard cap on total output frames. 0 = follow pose_video to end. |
| `vary_seed_per_segment` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `False` |  | OFF = same seed every segment. ON = adds segment index to seed. |
| `decode_tiled` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `False` |  | Decode each segment in tiles to save VRAM. |
| `low_vram` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `False` |  | ON = Purges CLIP / TextEncoder from VRAM before sampling. Saves 3-6 GB VRAM to prevent OOM. |
| `replacement_mode` | `BOOLEAN` | yes | `False` |  | True = Keeps original background. Composites the generated character back onto original background. |
| `mask_dilation` | `INT` | yes | `4` | -100 – 100 (step 1) | Expand (+) or contract (-) mask boundary. |
| `mask_feather` | `INT` | yes | `8` | 0 – 100 (step 1) | Blur mask edges for a seamless blend. |
| `reference_image` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | The character to animate. |
| `pose_video` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Frames carrying the motion. |
| `pose_video_mask` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Black & white mask of the character. |
| `clip_vision_output` | `CLIP_VISION_OUTPUT` | no | — |  |  |
| `positive_pose` | `CONDITIONING` | no | — |  |  |
| `clip_vision_output_pose` | `CLIP_VISION_OUTPUT` | no | — |  |  |
| `pose_strength` | `FLOAT` | no | `1.0` | 0.0 – 10.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `pose_start_percent` | `FLOAT` | no | `0.0` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `pose_end_percent` | `FLOAT` | no | `1.0` | 0.0 – 1.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `reference_image_strength` | `FLOAT` | no | `1.0` | 0.0 – 10.0 (step 0.01) |  |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |

| `images` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `frame_count` | `INT` |  |

## Onyx Prompt Generator

**Class:** `OnyxGeminiPromptNode` · **Category:** `utils` · output node

OFM Prompt Generator — analyze images or generate prompts with Gemini.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `mode` | Dropdown: `JSON Image Analysis`, `Style Transfer Prompt`, `Seedream Edit (2 face + 1 ref)`, `Seedream Edit (1 face + 1 ref)`, `Seedream Edit (2 face and body + 1 ref)`, `Seedream Edit (2 faces + 2 bodies + 1ref)`, `Custom Prompt` | yes | `JSON Image Analysis` |  |  |
| `provider` | Dropdown: `Gemini`, `Grok`, `Vertex` | yes | `Gemini` |  |  |
| `gemini_api_key` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  |  |
| `grok_api_key` | `STRING` | yes | `""` |  |  |
| `images` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  |  |
| `custom_prompt` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  |  |
| `vertex_json_folder` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | [VERTEX] Path to the folder containing service account JSON files (1 .json file = 1 project). Successive runs rotate through them to spread the per-project quota.<br>Pointing straight at a single .json also works. |
| `model` | Dropdown: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `grok-4.20-0309-reasoning`, `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning`, … (17 options) | no | `gemini-3.6-flash` |  | Model. The list shown follows the selected provider:<br>  Gemini / Vertex -> Gemini text models<br>  Grok            -> xAI models |
| `system_prompt` | `STRING` | no | `""` |  | System instruction, applied on all three providers (Gemini: systemInstruction \| Vertex: system_instruction \| Grok: a leading system message).<br>Paste a whole .md file here — it sets the persona and the rules, and stays separate from the per-run prompt.<br>On Gemini 3.x this is the main steering lever left, since temperature is deprecated there. |
| `thinking_level` | Dropdown: `default`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` | no | `default` |  | [Gemini / Vertex] Reasoning effort. 'default' sends nothing and leaves the model's own default in place.<br>minimal/low = faster and cheaper (extraction, classification)<br>medium/high = better on multi-step reasoning<br>Billed as output tokens. Ignored by Grok, and a level a model doesn't support is dropped rather than sent. |
| `temperature` | `FLOAT` | no | `1.0` | 0.0 – 2.0 (step 0.05) | Ignored by Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite — Google deprecated temperature/top_p/top_k there, and the node stops sending it rather than pretending it works.<br>Use system_prompt and thinking_level on those models. |
| `max_tokens` | `INT` | no | `8192` | 64 – 65536 (step 64) |  |
| `seed` | `INT` | no | `0` | 0 – 4294967295 |  |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `prompt` | `STRING` |  |

## Onyx Video Chain — Join

Concatenate the finished segments, and never run the ones the source cannot fill.

| `image_1` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Segment 1, whole. Always evaluated. |
| `audio_1` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  | Optional. Connect each sampler's audio output to get one continuous generated soundtrack. |
| `image_2` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Segment 2. Only evaluated when segments_needed >= 2; otherwise this whole branch is skipped. |
| `audio_2` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_3` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Segment 3. Only evaluated when segments_needed >= 3; otherwise this whole branch is skipped. |
| `audio_3` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_4` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Segment 4. Only evaluated when segments_needed >= 4; otherwise this whole branch is skipped. |
| `audio_4` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_5` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Segment 5. Only evaluated when segments_needed >= 5; otherwise this whole branch is skipped. |
| `audio_5` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  |  |
| `image_6` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | Segment 6. Only evaluated when segments_needed >= 6; otherwise this whole branch is skipped. |
| `audio_6` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  |  |

## Onyx Video Chain — Prepare

**Class:** `OnyxVideoChainPrepare` · **Category:** `video`

Hand out the guide tail and the reference slice for the current segment.

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `session_name` | `STRING` | yes | `chain` |  | One chain per name. Two workflows with different names advance independently. |
| `segment` | Dropdown: `39 frames (1.625 s)`, `90 frames (3.750 s)`, `141 frames (5.875 s)`, `192 frames (8.000 s)`, `243 frames (10.125 s)`, `294 frames (12.250 s)`, `345 frames (14.375 s)` | yes | `345 frames (14.375 s)` |  | Length of ONE generation. Every value here is on both H3 grids, so the audio stays in phase at the joints. 345 is H3's ceiling. |
| `overlap` | Dropdown: `39 (audio-exact)`, `22`, `5` | yes | `39 (audio-exact)` |  | How many frames of the previous segment are regenerated as a guide. More overlap = a steadier joint and less new footage per run. |
| `video_fps` | `FLOAT` | yes | `24.0` | 1.0 – 120.0 (step 0.01) |  |
| `reference_video` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | The full source video that carries the motion. It is sliced automatically: each segment receives the part that matches its own position on the timeline. |
| `reference_audio` | `AUDIO` | no | — |  | Sliced on the same window as the video. |
| `initial_frames` | `IMAGE` | no | — |  | What segment 1 uses as its guide — typically your swapped first frame. Left empty, segment 1 runs with no guide. |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `guide_frames` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `reference_slice` | `IMAGE` |  |
| `audio_slice` | `AUDIO` |  |
| `segment_index` | `INT` |  |
| `segment_frames` | `INT` |  |
| `overlap_frames` | `INT` |  |
| `is_first` | `BOOLEAN` |  |
| `info` | `STRING` |  |
